notes: The connector and every Takaro token/cloud setting remain dedicated-server-only. The separately packaged owned graphical-client companion has no Takaro credentials or direct cloud transport.

The companion protocol, required-mode enforcement, chat, inventory, death, and attributed-kill paths have exact live server/client/Takaro proof recorded in qa/2026-07-12-owned-companion-validation.md.
Client-reported observations are untrusted gameplay claims. They may enrich automation but must not become authoritative identity, security, anti-cheat, or moderation evidence.

In required mode, a missing, incompatible, or silent companion receives a visible explanation before delayed exact-peer disconnect. Version diagnostics include expected and actual protocol versions when available.
Dedicated-server records retain their historical artifact-pinned evidence. Client-reported live-supported records use the owned-companion validation run completed on 2026-07-12.
getPlayer is implemented by filtering the dedicated server player list, but its final Takaro response shape has not been independently live-proven, so it remains unsupported.

getPlayerLocation uses only a real ready-peer/public observation or a fresh 30-second player-keyed last-known observation. If neither exists, a required-coordinate payload with error is rejected by current Takaro Generic.requestFromServer rather than returned as a position.

getPlayerInventory is live-supported with a compatible companion and is sourced from bounded, canonical client-reported snapshots; without one, the server still refuses to fabricate an empty inventory.
giveItem creates server-owned world drops near the player's server-known position. These are collectible world objects, not a private inventory grant.

sendMessage is live-supported through a server-originated authenticated server-chat envelope and requires an active negotiated companion to render it in normal chat. The 2026-07-14 live run routed one Takaro request to one compatible peer, rendered an explicit opts.senderNameOverride of con in the client's normal chat history, and confirmed Takaro is used only when the value is missing or blank. It never falls back to a HUD overlay.
teleportPlayer routes Valheim's built-in RPC_TeleportTo to the server-known character ZDO owner.

Inbound chat is live-supported through the owned negotiated companion. Ordinary chat and configured commands were each persisted once, and a real tplist module command completed successfully without duplicating player-originated input.

Routed vanilla ChatMessage, Say, and OnDeath packets remain diagnostic-only. Implemented companion chat and death reports use the server-bound negotiated session and authoritative peer binding, while their gameplay contents remain untrusted client reports.

Player lifecycle frames are derived from dedicated-server player snapshots. Turn-3 Takaro eventSearch persisted two player-connected and two player-disconnected events; transport logs still claim only that a frame was written, not persistence acknowledgement.

listLocations is schema-fallback: turn 4 live-proved the official raw Generic Connector action/schema with 11293 nested server-owned locations in a 1815046-byte response, but Takaro 0c63cf1c Generic.listLocations throws NotImplementedError, so the standard Takaro route is unavailable pending upstream support.

getMapInfo and getMapTile are part of the exhaustive Takaro 0c63cf1c action list but unsupported at the dedicated-server-only boundary because Valheim exposes neither client map metadata nor rendered map tiles there.

Entity-killed is live-supported through the owned companion. Exact Takaro proof persisted one Greyling kill attributed to the bound player with weapon Unarmed; the implementation still treats this as an untrusted client gameplay report.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: banPlayer and unbanPlayer are live-supported. A live Takaro request wrote Steam_76561198000735875 into Valheim bannedlist.txt, disconnected the player without crashing the headless server, was read back by listBans with the accepted DTO shape, and was then removed so listBans returned an empty array.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: banPlayer discards the ban reason. A ban requested with reason 'acceptance test' was read back by Takaro listBans as reason ''. Valheim's native ban list stores only one player identifier per line, so the connector has nowhere to persist a reason.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: sendMessage ownership is client-reported, not server-owned. With companionMode=disabled the action returns companion_server_chat_unavailable, so outbound chat delivery depends on a negotiated companion on the receiving client.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: companionMode was verified live. disabled registers no companion RPC; required disconnects a vanilla client after the grace period with reason=MissingCompanion via the built-in Kicked RPC, leaving the dedicated server alive.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: kickPlayer is live-supported. A live Takaro request logged 'kicked Hehe (Steam_76561198000735875). Reason: acceptance kick test.', getPlayers dropped to zero, and the headless dedicated server stayed alive because the built-in Kicked RPC is used instead of a direct ZNet.Disconnect(peer).

2026-09-02 acceptance run: listItems and listEntities are live-supported through the standard Takaro route. Takaro does not request either action until its sync job runs, so a newly registered game server shows an empty catalog until then; triggering syncItems/syncEntities returned 821 item prefabs and 101 character prefabs, which Takaro persisted.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: shutdown is live-supported. A live Takaro request wrote its success response frame first, then logged 'executing scheduled shutdown on the Unity main thread'; Valheim performed a clean ZNet shutdown and the dedicated server process exited.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: Takaro shop deliveries inherit giveItem's world-drop semantics. A 5x Wood delivery spawned on the ground at the player's position and did not enter their inventory, so purchased goods are lootable by nearby players until collected. This is inherent to the dedicated-server boundary, not a connector defect.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: currency add/deduct, shop listing creation, inventory history, and radius player queries (including the negative case) were live-verified. Placing a shop order could not be tested because orders are placed as a linked player account and the admin session has none; the request never reaches the connector.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: restart resilience verified. After a dedicated-server restart the connector re-identified without config changes and events resumed, with a fresh player-connected persisted by Takaro and module commands still executing.
